name: Loki
whyHere: There is Precursor work in the Valley that nobody there understands, and you understand it, and that is dangerous for everyone including you.

inventory.name: Traveler's Pack

deeds.description: Spoke a true thing in the shape the Unlit could hear — and the elder of the Deep acknowledged it.

chronicle: Loki read the four spike entries with Tessvel Cairn in the Pressure-Routing Annex, named the pattern — something moves deeper into the lower routing channel with each morning pass — and proposed both channel access and a more personal arrangement; Tessvel confirmed the access, asked for time on the rest, and left Loki knowing exactly where to find them.

turns.summary: Loki enters the threshold of the Unlit Deep, Cy lamp-shuttered at heel, a grey-robed figure seated motionless by a pale blue flame ahead.
turns.narration:
The Unlit Deep is exactly what its name promises. The passage down from the city proper is not dramatic — a stair cut into old stone, lantern-brackets empty, the smell of cold mineral water and something older underneath it. Then the passage opens and the dark becomes a doctrine.

You are standing at the threshold of the Deep's outer chamber. The ceiling is too high to see. The floor is flat worked stone, worn smooth, and there is no source of light here that the Unlit did not allow. Somewhere further in, a single low flame burns in a bowl — pale blue, almost colorless — and by it you can make out a figure seated very still. Robed in grey, hands folded, facing away from you. The Unlit are gentle here. That is the thing the Umbrals will not say plainly but that their silence says for them: the Unlit are not violent. They simply want something that cannot be compromised with.

Cy is at your left heel, its many legs finding the worked stone without sound. Its lens is open wide — irising slowly, taking in the near-nothing light. It has not spoken since the stair. You have the sense it knows this place, or knows what was here before this place was what it is now. The lamp it carries is shuttered. You have not asked it to shutter the lamp. It did that on its own, before you reached the bottom step.

The seated figure has not moved. There is no one else visible, though the dark beyond the blue flame is absolute. The air is still. Whatever the Unlit have taken from the city — whoever they have brought here — is somewhere deeper than this room.

turns.summary: A second Unlit figure detaches from the shadows and blocks the exit — a hostile meeting, still conversational, but with intent.
turns.narration:
The figure by the blue flame does not move. Then the blue flame bends.

It bends toward you, all at once, without a draft — and in the moment it bends, a second shape detaches from the far wall. Not the seated figure. Something else. It was waiting in the dark where the stone meets the bracket-shadows, and you simply could not see it.

It is a person, or was. Grey-robed like the first, but standing, and the way it stands is wrong — too still in the shoulders, too precise in the feet. It speaks in a voice that is almost friendly.

"You brought a light-thing," it says. "We asked for no light-things."

Cy does not move. Its lens is open as wide as it goes, drinking the dark, watching.

The figure takes one step closer. The blue flame does not follow it. The seated figure by the bowl has not turned. This one is alone and it is between you and the passage out, and its hands are coming up from its robe — not with a weapon, exactly, but with an intention that makes the word weapon feel polite.

"You may leave the light-thing at the top of the stair," it says, still in that gentle voice. "Or you may leave something else."

turns.summary: Loki's misdirection found no purchase in the cult's absolute dark — the Standing Unlit waited it out and repeated the original demand.
turns.narration:
The Standing Unlit does not raise its voice. It does not need to. The hands come up from the robe — steady, open, patient — and the gentleness in them is the worst part. You reach for the false position, the wrong read, the misdirection that should buy you a step back toward the passage. The words form. The posture shifts. And the figure simply waits for all of it to finish.

When it speaks again, the voice is kind. "You are very good at that," it says. "We are not." It means something specific by 'not.' Not 'not good at seeing through it.' It means they do not have the reflex to be fooled. The dark, held this purely, leaves no room for a false signal to land. There is nothing here to catch the shape of it and believe. Your craft finds no purchase. It is like throwing a net into a room with nothing to catch.

You are still standing in the same spot. The passage out is still behind the figure. You have not been struck, not been touched. But you have spent something — energy, composure, the particular confidence that comes from knowing a trick will work — and the Standing Unlit has lost nothing at all. Cy's lens turns slowly toward you. The tiny irising of it is the only commentary it offers.

"Leave the light-thing at the stair," the Standing Unlit says. It is still gentle. "Or tell us what you came for. Those are the two things you can do here."

turns.player: Use The Better Story — give the Standing Unlit a version of why you are here that they can accept: the light-thing is a tool, not a doctrine, and you are not the Blaze.
turns.summary: Loki told the truth in a shape the Unlit could accept — Cy is older than doctrine, and it chose the dark itself — and the seated elder spoke for the first time, granting passage.
turns.narration:
You stop trying to trick the figure. You stop performing. You look at it — the Standing Unlit, hands raised from the robe, waiting with the patience of something that has never been in a hurry — and you simply tell the truth, but the truth shaped into something it can hold.

"Cy is a tool," you say. "An old one. Older than the Blaze, older than the doctrine that made the Blaze mean something. It came before all of that. It came before the choosing of sides." You let that sit for a moment. Then: "Its lamp is shuttered. Has been since the first step down. I did not ask it to do that. It did it on its own. Because it knows the difference between a light and a Light."

The Standing Unlit does not answer immediately. Its hands lower — not quickly, not warmly, but the way a door closes on a day that turned out fine. The silence it makes is different from the waiting-silence it was making before. This one has weight in it, the good kind, the kind that means something was heard.

Then the seated figure by the pale blue flame speaks for the first time. It does not turn around. Its voice is quieter than the Standing Unlit's, and precise in the way that old things are precise, worn smooth to their function. "Let the tool pass," it says. Then, after a pause: "And let the one who brought it say what they came to say."

The Standing Unlit steps aside.

*You feel it settle into you — a new steadiness. (Level 2: +1 attunement, +5 reserves, and growth to choose — a sub-attribute point and a skill point.)*

*✦ The Umbrals: +1 — reached the Unlit elder through honest framing rather than craft or coercion — demonstrated the kind of precision the dark respects.*

turns.player: Move forward but say nothing yet — read the chamber, read the elder, find the seam before speaking.
turns.summary: Loki approached the elder in silence, read the chamber, and found the oldest seam in the room before the elder spoke.
turns.narration:
You walk forward. Thirty feet of worked stone pass under your boots, each step quieter than the last, because the chamber asks for quiet and you have enough sense to give it.

The pale blue flame does not move this time. It burns in its stone bowl without bending, without reaching, a color that is almost not a color — less a light than the memory of one. By it, the elder sits. You can see the robe now, darker than the Standing Unlit's, worn at the hem. Hands rest on the knees. The face is still below the hood, but the posture is one you recognize: the posture of someone who has been waiting a very long time and has made their peace with waiting.

You look for the seam — the thing the chamber is built around, the thing the elder is holding. The stone is old and the wear is even, which means people have sat here before you, many of them, and they all sat in roughly the same spot. Not petitioners. Students, maybe. Or the surrendered. The blue flame has no wick you can find and no fuel-source you can name, and Cy's lens has been tracking it since you entered, slowly, the way Cy tracks things it recognizes and will not explain. One of the lantern-brackets on the left wall has a seam in the stone around it that does not match the age of the bracket — something was there before the bracket, and the bracket was fitted over it. That seam is the oldest thing in this room.

The elder's hands move once, a small gesture, like a period at the end of a sentence that has not yet been spoken. Then a voice — quieter than the Standing Unlit's, worn to its work — says: "Sit, if you want to. Or stand. It makes no difference here."

turns.player: Ask about the seam in the stone — the thing the bracket was fitted over. What was here before?
turns.summary: Loki asked about the seam in the stone — the elder declined, gently but absolutely, and the audience continues.
turns.narration:
You let the silence hold one beat longer, and then you ask. Your voice is quiet, and you aim it at the elder rather than the chamber. You say there is a seam in the stone behind the left-wall bracket — older than the bracket itself, older than the lantern that was never lit in it. You ask what was fitted there before.

The elder does not answer immediately. The pale blue flame burns without bending, and the hood does not rise. When the elder finally speaks, the voice is worn smooth to its purpose, and it is not unkind. "That question," the elder says, "belongs to the chamber. Not to a visitor."

It is not a rebuke. It is a door, closed gently. The elder's hands rest on the knees, unchanged. The posture says: the audience has not ended. Something else was invited here, and the seam was not it.

turns.player: Ask what the Unlit have brought down from the city — the real reason you came.
turns.summary: Loki asked directly about the taken person; the elder confirmed someone came willingly, is now in the inner chamber, and offered to let Loki ask whether they wish to leave.
turns.narration:
You ask. You keep your voice level and low, the way the chamber seems to want. You say that you heard something came down from the city. You say that the city is pretending it did not happen. You say that you came, in part, to know what that thing was.

The elder is quiet for a long moment. The pale blue flame burns without bending. Cy stands at your heel, lens turned toward the seated figure, irising once and then going still.

Then the elder speaks. The voice is the same worn smoothness as before — a tool that has been used for exactly one thing for a very long time. "Someone came," the elder says. "They did not come against their will. That is the part the city finds difficult to say." A small pause. "They are in the inner chamber. They have chosen the doctrine. The city sent no one for them, which tells you everything about whether the city truly believes they were taken."

The hands on the knees do not move. The hood does not rise. But something in the posture shifts — the way a door that was closed shifts when someone puts a hand on the far side of it. "You may ask whether they wish to be found," the elder says. "That question, I will allow. The answer belongs to them."

turns.player: Ask to speak with the person in the inner chamber — take the elder's offer.
turns.summary: Loki accepted the elder's offer and was granted entry to the inner chamber.
turns.narration:
You accept. You tell the elder that you would like to ask the question — whether the person in the inner chamber wishes to be found.

The elder's hands do not move on the knees. The pale blue flame burns without bending. Then the elder makes the small economical gesture you have seen once before, a hand-movement like a period at the end of a sentence, and says, "Then you may go in."

That is all. No instruction, no warning, no offer to accompany you. The passage behind the elder is a gap in the worked stone — darker than the chamber, which is itself very dark. You cannot see how far it goes. Cy presses close to your heel and its lens irises twice, reading something in the stonework you cannot read, and then it goes still again and waits for you to move.

The Standing Unlit does not follow. The elder does not rise. The blue flame burns on, and the outer chamber holds its breath behind you as you step toward the passage and the darker dark beyond it.

turns.player: Use prism site and move into the inner chamber.
turns.summary: Loki stepped into the inner chamber with Prism Sight active and found the taken person — seated, calm, and already waiting.
turns.narration:
You step through the gap in the worked stone and Prism Sight opens behind your eyes.

The inner chamber is smaller than the outer — a room meant for one or two, not an audience. The floor here is worn to the same evenness as outside, but in a narrower track, the path of someone who has paced, or sat for a long time in a single spot and then paced again. The walls are bare worked stone, and the ceiling is low enough that you could touch it.

There is no flame here. The only light is what seeps from the outer chamber, which is almost nothing. But Prism Sight fills in what the eye cannot find: heat traces, vivid and precise. A person is here — seated against the far wall, knees drawn up, head tilted to one side. The heat of their body reads clearly against the cold stone. They have been sitting in that spot long enough that the stone behind them has warmed a degree from their back. There is a second heat-trace on the floor beside them — a cup, recently set down, still warm at the rim.

The person's head lifts. They heard you come in. They say nothing yet, but you can see the shift in the heat-map of their face as they turn toward the sound of your step — eyes open, breath steady. Not afraid. Not surprised, exactly. Waiting, the way someone waits who has already decided what answer they will give, and is only waiting for the question.

turns.player: Give them The Better Story before you ask — name who you are and why you came, in a shape that makes the question easier to answer honestly
turns.summary: Loki gave the taken person an honest frame — who they are, why they came — and the person opened the door to the question.
turns.narration:
You crouch down so your eye level meets theirs. The cold of the floor comes through your knees at once.

You tell them your name. You say that you came down from the city not because the city sent you, but because you heard something and wanted to know if it was true. You say that you are not here to pull anyone back against their will. You say that you would like to ask one question, and that the answer — whatever it is — is theirs to give.

The person is quiet. Their head stays tilted toward you. Their hands, folded across their knees, do not move. Then they say, in a voice that is steadier than you expected for someone who has been sitting in the dark for however many days this has been: 'You can ask it.'

Cy stands at your heel. Its lens irises once toward the seated figure and then turns, briefly, to the floor beside them — to the cup that has gone almost cool — and then it is still.

turns.player: Use See the Made Thing on the cup or the room — let Cy's read and your own run together; find what the dark is built from
turns.summary: Loki read the cup and the chamber — the room predates the Unlit, someone down here made the cup by hand, and the taken person is fed and kept freely.
turns.narration:
You let your attention drop to the cup on the floor beside them. Cy's lens is already there, irised to its smallest aperture, reading.

See the Made Thing opens behind your eyes — not light, but construction. The cup is ceramic, unglazed, hand-shaped with the particular slight asymmetry of someone making it for themselves rather than for trade. The inner surface has a faint mineral ring at the waterline — not particulate, not nanite deposition, just dried water from a deep source. The clay itself reads as local. Someone down here made this. Not brought it. Made it.

The room is the same. You let the read move out from the cup to the walls, the floor, the ceiling. The stonework is old — older than the Unlit, you are certain of that. The worked-stone seam here is the same as the one you noticed in the outer chamber, the same tool-mark character, the same depth of cut. Whatever this room was before the Unlit found it, it was already here and already waiting. The Unlit did not build their doctrine into this space. They moved into something that was already suited to it. And the person seated against the far wall — their heat trace reads warm and well-fed against the stone. Someone is bringing them food. Someone is bringing them water from that deep source. They are being kept, not in the sense of prisoners, but in the sense of a sustained life. They are not starving into doctrine. They chose it with a full stomach.

The person's voice is quiet in the dark. "You said you have a question," they say.

turns.player: Ask the elder's question — do you wish to be found?
turns.summary: Loki put the elder's question to Sable in the inner chamber — the answer was no, given steadily, with a reason.
turns.narration:
You ask it plainly. You say: do you wish to be found?

The person across from you does not answer right away. They look toward where your voice came from — not at you, exactly, because the chamber is dark enough that looking and seeing are different things here. Then they let out a slow breath through their nose.

They say their name is Sable. They say it like a fact, not an introduction. Then they say: no.

The word sits in the cold air between you. It is not angry. It is not apologetic. It is the answer of someone who has already sat with the question for several days and arrived somewhere they feel steady.

Sable says they left the city because the city was too loud, and they do not mean noise. They mean the way everyone there knows what everything is for. Every object, every person, every hour. They came down here because the dark does not do that. They say this without heat, the way you'd explain a route you've walked before.

Cy clicks once, very quietly, at your heel. The lens stays on Sable's face.

turns.player: Offer Sable The Better Story before you go — give them a way to think about what they've chosen that isn't just doctrine
turns.summary: Loki gave Sable a way to carry their choice that was not doctrine and not reproach — and left the inner chamber with the answer the city cannot hear.
turns.narration:
You do not try to argue Sable back. You do not name a person waiting for them in the city, or a debt they owe to being found. You have the answer. What you do instead is offer them a frame for what they chose — not a lie, and not comfort, just a shape that holds.

You say that the city makes things legible. You say that is not the same thing as making them true. You say that choosing a thing the city cannot read is still choosing, and that there is a difference between hiding and arriving somewhere the light does not follow. You say you think Sable knows which one this is.

Sable is quiet for a moment. Then they say, quietly, that they did not expect that from someone who came down looking. Their voice does not warm exactly, but something in it settles, the way a piece of work settles when the last joint closes.

You stand. You tell Sable that if they ever want the city again, there are people who would hear from them without making it a return. Then you step back toward the faint pale blue that seeps under the passage gap, Cy at your heel, and leave the inner chamber to the cold and the dark and Sable's choice.

turns.player: Bring the answer back to the elder before you leave — tell them what Sable said, and what you said, and ask if there is anything else the elder would have you carry out
turns.summary: Loki brought Sable's honest answer back to the elder — name, reason, and the frame left behind — and the elder acknowledged that the coming and the leaving without taking was itself the deed.
turns.narration:
You step back through the gap into the outer chamber. The pale blue flame is exactly where you left it. The elder is exactly where you left them. You have the sense that this is always true.

You tell them what Sable said. You give them the name first, because Sable offered it freely and you see no reason to withhold it. You tell them the answer was no, given steadily, without hesitation or apology. Then you tell them what you said in return — not all of it, just the shape of it: that there is a difference between hiding and arriving somewhere the light does not follow. You do not embellish. The dark here does not reward embellishment.

The elder listens without moving. When you finish, there is a short silence. Then they say, in that worn-smooth voice: 'You did not try to take them.' It is not quite a question. They make a small economical gesture with one hand — not pointing anywhere, just completing a thought. 'That is what we would have you carry,' they say. 'That you came, you asked, and you left the answer where it landed.' They are quiet for another moment. Then they say: 'The elder of the outer chamber thanks you for carrying it honestly.'

The Standing Unlit near the passage has not moved. Cy is at your heel, lens at a careful half-aperture. The passage back up to the city is open. The elder does not rise to see you out.

turns.player: Ask the Elder to teach you one thing - how to make the unlit blue flame.
turns.summary: Loki asked the elder to teach the making of the pale blue flame — and was told, without hostility, that the flame is not a thing that can be taught.
turns.narration:
You ask the elder directly. You say you would like to learn one thing before you go — how to make the blue flame. You gesture toward the bracket on the wall, where the pale fire sits without a wick and without an explanation.

The elder does not move. They do not look at the flame. When they speak, their voice is worn smooth and unhurried, and it is not unkind.

They say that the flame is not theirs to teach. They say this is not a refusal of you, exactly — it is a statement of category. The flame belongs to the dark. The dark does not have a curriculum. What you are asking is the wrong shape of question for the thing you are pointing at.

Then they are quiet, and the quiet closes the subject. Cy's lens irises once at the bracket, measuring, and does not open any further. The pale blue flame continues its slow, sourceless burn, and you are no closer to understanding what it is made of.

turns.player: Use See the Made Thing on the flame itself — read its construction before you leave
turns.summary: Loki attempted to read the pale blue flame's construction — and found nothing to read.
turns.narration:
You turn your attention to the flame before you go. You have read cups, rooms, seams in stone — the construction of things is your ground. You let See the Made Thing settle into focus, the way you always do, looking for the joinery, the made shape, the point where intention meets material.

There is nothing to catch. Not because the flame hides itself — it does not. It sits exactly where it is, burning without a wick, giving off a light that is more like the absence of dark than the presence of anything. But the craft finds no edge to read. A made thing has seams. This has no seams. A made thing begins somewhere and ends somewhere. This does not seem to have begun.

Cy irises once at the bracket, then closes the lens and does not open it again. This is, you have learned, Cy's way of saying that it also found nothing, and that finding nothing is the more interesting result.

The elder does not look up. They do not say anything. They did not need to warn you — the flame already said what it had to say, which is that it is not available for this kind of conversation.

turns.player: Use the better story.  Tell the elder that if you know the right question to ask, and you learn the secret of the blue flame... you can bring it's unlight to the world as you travel.
turns.summary: Loki offered the elder a frame — not a request to be taught, but a promise to carry the right question outward; the elder gestured to the seam in the stone and named it older than the flame, older than the Unlit, and waiting.
turns.narration:
You do not ask again. You offer instead.

You tell the elder that you understand the flame is not a lesson. You tell them that you are not asking to be taught a technique. What you are asking is a different shape of thing: you want to know the right question. Because if you know the right question, you say, you can carry it with you. You have seen, already tonight, that the dark travels further than most people believe. You travel. You go into places where the light reaches too hard and crowds things out. If you carried the right question about the blue flame, you might find, somewhere in the world, the answer that fits it — and then you might bring that unlight to places that have never had it. You say this plainly, without flourish, because the elder has shown you that flourish finds no grip here.

The elder is quiet for a long moment. Then they say: the question is not yours yet to carry, but you have shown you know how to carry a question honestly. They lift one hand — the first real movement they have made — and they gesture, not at the flame, but at the seam in the stone beside the bracket. They say: that is older than the flame, and older than us, and it has been waiting for someone to ask the wrong question of the right thing. Then they lower the hand and are still again. The subject does not close, exactly. It rests.

Cy irises twice, a fast double-blink it only does when something does not fit any category it holds. It does not speak. But it has been looking at the seam since the elder's hand moved, and it has not looked away.

*✦ The Umbrals: +0.99 — Offered the elder a true shape for what was being asked — not a request for craft, but a promise to carry the right question outward honestly; the elder acknowledged it with their first real movement (held at the band's edge).*

turns.player: Examine the seam the elder just indicated — run See the Made Thing along it, this time with the question the elder's gesture shaped
turns.summary: Loki read the seam with See the Made Thing — found it is a door, cut with purpose, older than the Unlit and older than the flame, made for something to pass through.
turns.narration:
You turn from the flame to the seam. The elder's hand has settled back into their lap, but the gesture lingers in the air — it pointed at something specific, and you let that specificity guide you.

You bring See the Made Thing to bear the same way you did with the flame, but you ask a different question this time. Not what is this and how was it made — but what question does this answer? The seam is a straight vertical line in the worked stone beside the bracket, running from the floor to a hand-span above your eye level. It is cleaner than a natural crack and older than the bracket that now sits beside it. The stone on either side of it is the same stone, but the seam itself is a gap between two intentions — two separate placements of rock that were meant to meet here and were meant to be opened again.

The craft finds something. Not joinery exactly — not the fingerprint of a maker's hand, not the seam of an illusion or a lie — but a shape of purpose. It is a door, or it was meant to be one. The frame is cut for something to pass through. The cut is very old, and it is not the Unlit's work, and it is not the Precursor work Cy would recognize. It predates the bracket. It predates the pale blue flame that now burns beside it. Whatever this passage was made for, it was made before anyone in this chamber decided what the chamber was for.

Cy makes a small sound — a single click, low and slow. It has not moved its lens away from the seam since the elder's hand pointed at it, and it does not move it now. Beside the passage to the stairs, the Standing Unlit is absolutely still.

turns.player: Put your hand to the seam — feel the edge of it, see if it responds to pressure or to the right kind of attention
turns.summary: Loki pressed a hand to the ancient seam beside the bracket — felt precision, intention, and a faint waiting vibration; the door is real, but it did not open. Cy extended one foreleg toward it and held still. The Unlit Deep has given everything it will give this visit.
turns.narration:
You press your palm flat against the seam. The stone is cold — the deep, steady cold of rock that has never been warm, not even in summer. The cut edge of the seam is precise under your fingertip. Whoever made this did not rush. You can feel where the tool changed direction, three times, in a line no wider than a knife's edge.

Then something shifts. Not movement — there is no movement. It is more like a held breath releasing slightly, the way a door will settle when the season changes and the wood contracts. Your hand does not pass through. The seam does not open. But the stone along the cut edge carries a faint vibration, barely there, the kind a thing makes when it is waiting for the right pressure in the right place. Not today's pressure. Not this morning's asking.

Cy makes two clicks in close succession. Its lens, which has not moved from the seam since the elder's gesture, irises down to a pinpoint and then opens again. It does not speak. But it shifts its weight to two legs and very carefully extends one foreleg toward the lower portion of the seam — stopping just short of touching, holding there, precise and patient.

The elder has not moved. The Standing Unlit has not moved. The pale blue flame offers nothing but its own light. The seam is real, purposeful, and waiting — and this morning is not the morning it opens.

turns.player: Ask Cy to help you open the door - use prism site to aid you.
turns.summary: Loki and Cy worked the seam together — Prism Sight finding the warmth-point low in the cut, Cy tapping the floor at the base to confirm — and learned the door's asking-point is near the floor, though it did not open. The Unlit Deep has given what it will give this visit.
turns.narration:
You look down at Cy. The lens is already wide, one foreleg still extended toward the lower seam, held just short of contact — it has been holding that posture for long enough that it has formed a conclusion of some kind, and conclusions in Cy read as posture before they read as sound.

You bring Prism Sight to bear alongside it. Heat-reading is not what this door wants, but you are not trying to read heat. You are trying to read attention — where Cy's foreleg is pointing, where the vibration you felt under your palm is strongest, where the seam's precision bends. The lattice here is dense and crowded, nine signals where you want one, and the Sight runs through it the way a voice runs through a crowded room: present, but frayed at the edges. You get a shape, not a certainty. The lowest third of the seam is warmer than the rest — not warm as a body is warm, but warmer as a mechanism is warm when it has been asked to do something recently and has been waiting to do it again.

Cy gives two clicks. Then a third, which is not its usual. It sets its foreleg down and taps the floor once, precisely, at the base of the seam. It does not touch the stone itself. The elder has not moved. The Standing Unlit has not moved. The chamber holds its breath.

The door does not open. But the vibration under your palm shifts when Cy taps — the same faint waiting quality, but directed now, pulled toward the base. The craft found you something real: the mechanism, if there is a mechanism, is low. The asking point, if there is one, is near the floor. That is more than you came here with. It is not an open door.

facts: [d1] The Annex is narrow, well-lit, and entirely open — a high east window sends light straight down the table and the gate is visible from the passage outside. No privacy. One chair. Cy flagged an anomalous resonance signature in the doorway and would not classify it.

[d1] The Annex substrate is saturated — signal density from the surrounding works makes fine Falsecraft difficult; a partial attention-deflection was the best the lattice would allow. A full shroud is not possible here without more power or a different approach.

[d1] First spike entry read via See the Made Thing: the particulate count rose before the intake valve opened for the morning cycle — the anomaly is in water already inside the works, not in the river coming in.

[d1] Fourth spike entry: nine-minute pressure-drop before particulate — the interval has grown evenly from four minutes (entry two) to six (entry three) to nine (entry four). Something moves through the lower routing channel before each morning cycle, and it is going deeper or slower each pass. The…

pressure-routing-annex.label: Pressure-Routing Annex
facts: [d1] Something beneath the Annex doorway is older than the building — pre-Annex, pre-current works, the impression surviving through lattice noise before it was drowned. Could not be classified. Cy aimed its lens at the spot and did not explain.

[d1] The threshold holds a circular boundary-impression — old enough that the substrate has grown around it like scar tissue. Not a mechanism: a boundary. Something was meant to stop here, or to be stopped. The shape is pre-Annex, pre-works. Function still unread.
[d1] Second spike entry: a pressure-drop in the lower routing channel preceded the particulate count by exactly four minutes — something moved through the channel before the morning intake cycle ran.

[d1] A low, clean chord rose through the floor of the Annex — a single note, not the works, not the pressure-wheel. Older. Cy's lens turned toward the stone and watched. Tessvel heard it. The sound and the terminus-seal may be the same thing briefly speaking.

terminus-seals-beneath-valley.label: Terminus-Seals Beneath the Valley
facts: [d1] Cy has catalogued four terminus-seals in the old service-ways beneath the valley — pre-Transition boundary-marks designed to hold a limit against propagation. Three are intact. One is not. Cy did not say which.

[d1] Something beneath the Annex floor hummed a single chord and went quiet — the sensation came up through the stone. Cy watched the floor without explanation. The chord may be one of the four terminus-seals briefly activating, or briefly failing.

the-unlit-deep.label: The Unlit Deep
facts: [d1] you have walked here
[d1] The outer chamber is worked stone, ceiling invisible, lit only by a single pale blue flame the Unlit allow. Cy shuttered its lamp before the bottom step — unprompted, without explanation.
[d1] The inner chamber is now accessible — the elder granted passage after Loki's honest account. The blue flame and the seated elder are the heart of the outer space; what lies beyond is unread.

[d1] The outer chamber floor is worn evenly across its full width — many visitors, all sitting in the same spot. The lantern-bracket on the left wall has a seam in the surrounding stone that predates the bracket itself; something else was fitted there before it. The blue flame has no visible wick or…

[d1] The inner chamber is smaller than the outer — a room for one or two. The floor is worn in a narrower track than the outer chamber: the path of someone who has sat long and occasionally paced. Ceiling low enough to touch. No flame. Cold stone that holds a body's warmth once given it.

[d1] The inner chamber predates the Unlit — the stonework and tool-marks are older than the doctrine, the same character as the seam in the outer chamber. The Unlit did not build this space; they moved into something already suited to it.

[d1] The elder refused to teach the making of the pale blue flame — said it is not theirs to teach, that it belongs to the dark, and that the question itself is the wrong shape. The flame is not craft as Loki understands craft.

[d1] The pale blue flame has no construction that See the Made Thing can read — no seams, no point of origin, no edge. It is not hiding its joinery; the joinery simply does not exist in a form the craft can find. Cy closed its lens and said nothing, which is Cy's conclusion that the absence is itself…

the-unlit.label: The Unlit
facts: [d1] A cult of the pure dark-pole. They are described as gentle. They want something that cannot be compromised with. The Umbrals go quiet when asked about them. They have apparently taken someone from the city.

[d1] A second Unlit figure was concealed in the bracket-shadows of the outer chamber — patient, skilled at stillness, and gentle in address even while blocking the exit. They object to Cy's lamp on principle and call it a 'light-thing.'

[d1] Misdirection and false signals find no purchase in their space — not because they are perceptive, but because the pure dark they hold leaves nothing for a false read to land on. The craft simply has nothing to catch.

[d1] The Better Story — truth in the shape they can carry — reaches the Unlit where misdirection cannot. They are not fooled by performance, but they can be moved by honest framing. The elder spoke for the first time when Loki named Cy as older than doctrine, and the Standing Unlit stepped aside.

standing-unlit.label: Standing Unlit
facts: [d1] Cult member, guardian of the outer chamber
[d1] [while away] The guardian remained at their post through all three days without incident — no visitors, no orders from within, nothing to act on.

unlit-elder.label: Unlit Elder
facts: [d1] Seated elder of the Unlit Deep's outer chamber

[d1] The elder declined to speak about the seam in the stone — 'that question belongs to the chamber, not to a visitor.' The refusal was gentle but absolute, with no hostility in it. The seam exists and is real; the elder knows what it is and has chosen not to say.

[d1] The elder named the deed: that Loki came, asked, and left the answer where it landed. They called this what they would have Loki carry. The elder thanks by naming the act, not by gesture or gift.

[d1] The elder gestured at the seam in the stone beside the blue-flame bracket and named it: older than the flame, older than the Unlit, and waiting for someone to ask the wrong question of the right thing. The elder did not explain further. The subject rests, not closed.

the-taken-from-the-city.label: The Taken From the City
facts: [d1] The person came willingly — the elder was explicit. The city sent no one to retrieve them, which the elder reads as proof the city knows this. The person is in the inner chamber and has chosen the doctrine. The elder permits Loki to ask whether they wish to be found.
[d1] The person accepted Loki's honest framing — name, purpose, no coercion — and said 'You can ask it.' The elder's permitted question has not yet been put, but the ground for it is clear.

[d1] The cup beside them was made here from local clay — someone in the Unlit Deep is making things by hand. The taken person is fed from a deep water source and kept freely. They are not being starved or pressured into doctrine; they came with a full stomach and are staying the same way.

[d1] Their name is Sable. They do not wish to be found. They left the city because the city makes everything — objects, people, hours — legible and purposeful, and they could not breathe inside that. The choice to come to the Unlit Deep was entirely their own.

[d1] Before leaving, Loki offered Sable a frame for what they chose — the difference between hiding and arriving somewhere the light does not follow. Sable said they had not expected that. The parting was settled and unhostile. No promise of return was made; no door was closed.

[d1] The person is in the inner chamber — seated against the far wall, knees drawn up, calm and unhurried. They have been there long enough to warm the stone at their back. A cup, recently set down, is beside them. They are not afraid. They heard Loki enter and turned toward the sound — waiting, the…

the-seam-in-the-unlit-stone.label: The Seam Beside the Bracket
facts: [d1] Named by the Unlit Elder as older than the flame, older than the Unlit themselves, and waiting for someone to ask the wrong question of the right thing. Cy locked its lens on it and has not looked away. This is the second stonework of this character in the Unlit Deep — the inner chamber walls bear…

[d1] See the Made Thing confirmed it is a door-frame — cut with clear purpose, made for something to pass through. It predates the pale blue flame, predates the bracket beside it, and predates the Unlit's occupation of the chamber. The craft found no maker's fingerprint it could name. The purpose-shape…

[d1] Physical contact confirmed: the seam is cut with precision — the tool changed direction exactly three times. Under a hand's pressure, it gives a faint vibration, like a thing waiting for the right asking. It did not open. The morning was not the right pressure. Cy extended one foreleg toward the…

[d1] Prism Sight and Cy's combined attention found the seam's asking-point: the lowest third runs warmer than the rest — the quality of a mechanism recently queried and still waiting to answer. Cy tapped the floor at the seam's base to confirm. The door did not open, but the asking-point is now located.

vessa-torquen.name: Vessa Torquen
vessa-torquen.role: Quay-side Enginewright conducting seasonal water-intake assessment — first point of contact between Pressureholt and Loki
vessa-torquen.voiceHints: Talks the way she works — practical, sequenced, no wasted motion. Warm without being soft; she will laugh at something genuinely funny and then immediately write it in a margin. Asks two clarifying questions before forming an opinion and means both of them. When something does not fit the system she is mapping, she does not dismiss it — she opens a new column.
knowledge: Pressureholt's full water-intake network: draw points, filter grades, seasonal pressure variances, every corroded join that has been on the list since last thaw
How to read a stranger's weight-distribution and tool-calluses as fluently as a pressure gauge
The Precursor intake manifolds sunk in the harbour bed — their geometry is not quite Gearlands-standard and she has been quietly noting discrepancies for three seasons
Which Enginewrights on the quay are capable and which are capable of looking capable — she knows the difference
vessa-torquen.wants: To complete a comprehensive systems map of Pressureholt's water infrastructure before the spring surge peaks — and, now that Loki has walked into her sampling radius, to understand exactly what kind of variable she is dealing with before she files a report or says a word to anyone senior.
vessa-torquen.fears: That the Precursor manifold anomalies she has been noting are load-bearing to something far larger than a water system, and that by the time she has enough data to prove it, the decision will already have been made by someone who did not take the measurements.

Her hands are the largest thing about her — capable, unhurried, already holding a grease-pencil and a folded intake log when Loki first sees her. She looks up from the gauge without startlement, as though she already wrote 'stranger arrives' in the margin.
vessa-torquen.currentActivity: Crouching at the number-three draw point, comparing this season's flow-pressure reading against last year's log, when she clocks Loki. She does not stop writing. She finishes the entry first.

chronicleCache.text: You have become someone the town can no longer quite contain — restless in a way that has nothing to do with youth and everything to do with the particular ache of a man who suspects the world is larger than the shape he was handed. The one deed that has begun to matter: you descended into the dark where the Unlit make their slow, lightless congress, and instead of performing certainty you spoke a true thing in the shape they could actually receive — and the elder acknowledged you, which is not nothing, which is in fact quite a lot. Tessvel Cairn is becoming the gravity you orbit when you're home, the courting between you still new enough to carry heat and weight — her presence a specific warmth you find yourself turning toward the way a cold man turns toward a window where the sun is. The question that drives you, beneath all of it, is the one with no clean answer yet: where did you come from, and what are the Veilwrights and the Umbrals and the Horizon-Walkers to that story? You don't know. You're going to find out.

picks.why: You're already a social 15 character built around The Better Story and The Misdirect — Harmonic Voice extends that same verbal dominance into emotion-management, letting you soften rooms before the deception lands rather than recovering after it goes wrong.

Silver_tongue and charmer are your recognised aptitudes, yet your kit is all fabrication and concealment with no tool for open negotiation — Mediator's Tongue gives you a craft for the moments your deceits are exposed and you need to talk your way through the truth.

See the Made Thing is your most-used craft by a mile — you're constantly reading situations — but Hunter's Strike and The False Target go untouched because you're not a fighter; Blend In lets you act on what you observe by simply vanishing into a crowd, a pure social-stealth tool that fits how you actually play.

See the Made Thing is your signature (10 uses) and you clearly play a reader of hidden truths; Prism Sight deepens that exact function — heat traces, concealed marks, lies of light — and directly advances Appetite-Sense, your declared aspiration around perceiving what others hide.

_suggestCache.note: Every pick this level lives in the social-cerebral lane you already inhabit — the question is whether you deepen your influence (Harmonic Voice), fill the negotiation gap (Mediator's Tongue), extend your stealth-social reach (Blend In), or double down on your perception signature toward your Appetite-Sense aspiration (Prism Sight).
